sections.title: Section A · Textbook-style questions
sections.note: Short questions like the exercises in the NCERT textbook.

questions.text: Look at the capital letters $A, B, C, D, E, H, K, M, T, U, V, W, X, Y$. (a) Which have a standing (vertical) line of symmetry? (b) Which have a sleeping (horizontal) line of symmetry? (c) Which have both?
questions.answer: (a) $A, H, M, T, U, V, W, X, Y$ (b) $B, C, D, E, H, K, X$ (c) $H$ and $X$

questions.text: Copy each figure and draw all its lines of symmetry. How many lines does each figure have?

picture.caption: Draw all the lines of symmetry of each figure.

answerPicture.caption: Red lines: the lines of symmetry.

questions.text: Give one example of a figure with: (a) no line of symmetry (b) exactly one line (c) exactly two lines (d) infinitely many lines.
questions.answer: (a) a parallelogram or a triangle with three different sides (b) an isosceles triangle or a kite (c) a rectangle or a rhombus (d) a circle

questions.text: Find the angle and the order of rotational symmetry of: (a) a square (b) an equilateral triangle (c) a regular pentagon (d) the letter $Z$.
questions.answer: (a) $90^\circ$, order $4$ (b) $120^\circ$, order $3$ (c) $72^\circ$, order $5$ (d) $180^\circ$, order $2$

questions.text: A figure looks the same after every turn of $45^\circ$. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
questions.answer: Order $= 360^\circ \div 45^\circ = 8$

questions.text: True or false? (a) Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry. (b) The diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry. (c) A parallelogram has rotational symmetry. (d) A figure of order $1$ has rotational symmetry.
questions.answer: (a) True (b) False: only the lines through the mid-points of opposite sides work (c) True: order $2$ (d) False: order $1$ means it fits only after a full turn

questions.text: Copy and complete the table: number of lines of symmetry and order of rotational symmetry of a square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, kite and isosceles trapezium.
questions.answer: Square $4$, order $4$; rectangle $2$, order $2$; rhombus $2$, order $2$; parallelogram $0$, order $2$; kite $1$, order $1$; isosceles trapezium $1$, order $1$

questions.text: In a seven-segment display (as on a calculator), which digits $0$–$9$ have a sleeping (horizontal) line of symmetry?
questions.answer: The digits $0, 1, 3$ and $8$. The top half of each one is a mirror image of the bottom half.

sections.title: Section B · Complete the figure
sections.note: The red line is a line of symmetry. Draw the other half on squared paper. Questions 13–16 are interactive.

questions.text: The red line is a line of symmetry. Copy the figure on squared paper and complete the other half.
questions.answer: Reflect each corner: a corner $k$ squares left of the mirror goes $k$ squares to the right, at the same height. The result is a house shape.

answerPicture.caption: Blue: given half. Orange: the reflected half.

questions.text: The red line is a line of symmetry. Complete the figure below the line.
questions.answer: Each corner goes to the same distance below the line. The completed figure is a fish shape.

questions.text: The red slanting line is a line of symmetry. Complete the figure on the other side of the line.
questions.answer: For a slanting mirror through opposite corners of the squares, the image of the corner $(x, y)$ is $(y, x)$: count the squares across and down, and swap them.

questions.text: Both red lines are lines of symmetry. One quarter of the figure is given. Complete the whole figure.
questions.answer: Reflect the quarter in the standing line, then reflect both parts in the sleeping line. The full figure has $2$ lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order $2$.

questions.text: Interactive: colour the squares on the right of the mirror to complete the picture. Press "Check".
questions.answer: The right half is the mirror image of the left half: each coloured square has a partner at the same height and the same distance from the mirror.

questions.text: Interactive: colour the squares below the mirror to complete the picture. Press "Check".
questions.answer: Each square above the line has a partner at the same distance below it.

questions.text: Interactive: complete the picture in the slanting mirror. Press "Check".
questions.answer: The square in row $r$, column $c$ goes to row $c$, column $r$.

questions.text: Interactive: there are two mirrors. Complete all four quarters. Press "Check".
questions.answer: Reflect the quarter in the standing mirror and then reflect both parts in the sleeping mirror. Each square has $3$ partners.

sections.title: Section C · Rotational symmetry
sections.note: Turn the figure in your mind, or trace it and turn the tracing.

questions.text: Find the angle and the order of rotational symmetry of each figure.
questions.answer: (a) $90^\circ$, order $4$ (b) $120^\circ$, order $3$. Neither figure has a line of symmetry, because each blade leans to one side.

picture.caption: Find the angle and order of rotational symmetry.

questions.text: Draw a figure that has rotational symmetry of order $2$ but no line of symmetry.
questions.answer: A parallelogram that is not a rectangle or a rhombus, or the letters $S$, $N$ or $Z$.

questions.text: A rangoli looks the same after a turn of $60^\circ$ but not after a turn of $30^\circ$. Find its order. Will it look the same after $240^\circ$?
questions.answer: Order $= 360^\circ \div 60^\circ = 6$. Yes: $240^\circ = 4 \times 60^\circ$.

questions.text: Which of these look the same after a quarter turn ($90^\circ$): a square, a rectangle, a circle, the letter $H$, a plus sign $+$?
questions.answer: A square, a circle and a plus sign. A rectangle and $H$ need a half turn.

sections.title: Section D · Higher-order thinking
sections.note: Think, try an example, then answer.

questions.text: Some squares are shaded. What is the smallest number of squares you must shade so that the red line becomes a line of symmetry?
questions.answer: The left half has $5$ shaded squares: $3$ in the top row and $2$ below the first square. Their mirror images are the last $3$ squares of the top row and $2$ squares below the last square. $2$ of the top-row images are already shaded. So shade the last square of the top row and the $2$ squares below it: $3$ squares.

picture.caption: Add the fewest squares so that the red line is a line of symmetry.

questions.text: A figure has rotational symmetry of order $4$. Must it have $4$ lines of symmetry?
questions.answer: No. A windmill with $4$ blades that lean the same way has order $4$ but no line of symmetry. A square has both.

questions.text: Write a word of four or more capital letters that has a standing line of symmetry, and one that has a sleeping line of symmetry.
questions.answer: Standing: $TOOT$, $MOM$, $WOW$ (each letter has a standing line and the word reads the same both ways). Sleeping: $BOOK$, $DECK$, $CHECK$ (each letter has a sleeping line).

questions.text: An equilateral triangle is cut along one line of symmetry. Describe the two pieces. Can you join them in another way to make a new figure with a line of symmetry?
questions.answer: The two pieces are right-angled triangles that are mirror images of each other. Put their longest sides together to make a kite-like shape, or put their shortest sides together to make an isosceles triangle. Both new shapes have a line of symmetry.

questions.text: Raj says: "If a figure has two lines of symmetry, it must also have rotational symmetry." Check this with a rectangle, a rhombus and a square. Is Raj right?
questions.answer: Yes. A rectangle and a rhombus have $2$ lines and order $2$. A square has $4$ lines and order $4$. A fold in one line and then a fold in the other line acts like a half turn.

sections.title: Section E · Case studies
sections.note: Read the situation and answer each part.

questions.text: Case study: Meena makes a rangoli for Diwali with $8$ petals round a centre. The petals are red and yellow, one after the other.
questions.answer: (a) A turn of $45^\circ$ moves a red petal to a yellow place, so it does not look the same. A turn of $90^\circ$ does. Angle $90^\circ$, order $4$. (b) Order $8$, angle $45^\circ$. (c) $4$ lines: each line goes through the middles of two opposite petals of the same colour. (d) $8$ lines.

picture.caption: A rangoli with 8 petals in two colours.

parts: (a) Find the angle and the order of rotational symmetry.
(b) Meena colours all the petals red. What are the new angle and order?
(c) How many lines of symmetry does the two-colour rangoli have?
(d) How many lines of symmetry does the all-red rangoli have?

questions.text: Case study: Ravi makes a kite for Sankranti. It has two sticks: the long stick $AC$ and the cross stick $BD$. $AB = AD$ and $CB = CD$.
questions.answer: (a) $1$ line: the long stick $AC$. (b) No. Folding along $BD$ puts $A$ on a point inside, not on $C$. (c) Yes: the tail hangs from $C$, which is on the line $AC$, so the picture stays symmetric. (d) No. After a half turn, the short sides go to the bottom.

picture.caption: A kite ABCD with its two sticks AC and BD.

parts: (a) How many lines of symmetry does the kite have? Name the line.
(b) Is the cross stick $BD$ a line of symmetry?
(c) Ravi ties a tail at $C$. Does the kite stay symmetric?
(d) Does the kite have rotational symmetry?

sections.title: Section F · Assertion and reason
sections.note: Decide whether each statement is true, and whether the reason explains the assertion.

questions.text: Assertion (A): A rectangle has $2$ lines of symmetry. Reason (R): The diagonals of a rectangle are its lines of symmetry. Choose: (i) both true, R explains A (ii) both true, R does not explain A (iii) A true, R false (iv) A false, R true.
questions.answer: (iii) A is true, but R is false. The lines of symmetry go through the mid-points of opposite sides, not along the diagonals.

questions.text: Assertion (A): A regular hexagon has rotational symmetry of order $6$. Reason (R): Its angle of symmetry is $60^\circ$ and $360^\circ \div 60^\circ = 6$. Choose (i), (ii), (iii) or (iv) as in the question above.
questions.answer: (i) Both are true, and R explains A.
